text:
UN General Assembly resolutions are generally non-binding recommendations under Articles 10 and 13 of the UN Charter and are not a formal source under Article 38 of the ICJ Statute. They can be evidence of customary international law or *opinio juris*, as the ICJ held in *Nicaragua* (1986), but their weight depends on content, voting, and supporting state practice. The shared note is wrong: a resolution is never conclusive proof of custom just because nearly all States are represented when it is adopted.

CONFIDENCE: 88
